exposure: mode of delivery in previous pregnancy
mode of delivery in previous pregnancy (vaginal birth, cesarean section before the second stage of labor, second stage cesarean section)
mode of delivery in a previous pregnancy
cesarean section before the second stage of labor
cohort: 18,253 women who had two consecutive deliveries in the participating hospitals between January 2012 and January 2022
finding: Compared to vaginal birth, second-stage cesarean section was significantly associated with an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth and early spontaneous preterm birth in the subsequent pregnancy.
mod_finding: Second-stage cesarean section significantly increased the risk of spontaneous preterm birth (aOR, 3.23; 95% CI, 2.02-5.17; P = 0.003) and early spontaneous preterm birth (aOR, 3.59; 95% CI, 2.01-5.19; P <0.001) in the subsequent pregnancy compared to vaginal birth.
gest_age: Preterm birth was defined as birth before 37 weeks of gestation.
